# `Q-1-28` — Conflicting Merge Operations

> A YAML tag specifies both `prefer` and `concat` — only one merge
> operation is allowed per tag.

## What this means

When Quarto merges configuration across layers, each tagged value
can declare one of two merge strategies: `prefer` (this value
overrides the same key in earlier layers) or `concat` (this value
is appended to the same key in earlier layers). The two strategies
are mutually exclusive — a single value cannot both override and
append at once — so a tag may name at most one.

This error fires when a tag combines both `prefer` and `concat`,
in either order: `!prefer_concat`, `!concat_prefer`, or any tag
with both components mixed in among other component names.

## Why this happens

The two situations:

- **Hand-construction.** Someone deliberately wrote both operations
  into a single tag, perhaps trying to express a hybrid behavior
  Quarto does not offer.
- **Merging of edited tags.** A configuration that started with one
  operation had the other appended by a later edit, instead of
  replacing the first.

## How to fix

Decide which behavior you want and remove the other component.

If you want the later layer's value to **override** earlier layers,
keep `prefer`:

```yaml
authors: !prefer_md
  - "[Pat](mailto:pat@example.com)"
```

If you want the later layer's value to **append** to earlier layers,
keep `concat`:

```yaml
authors: !concat_md
  - "[Sam](mailto:sam@example.com)"
```

If you really need both behaviors for different parts of the value,
restructure the configuration so that each part of the value is
tagged separately.
